title: Find All Anagrams in a String
statement: Return every start index in `s` where the substring of length len(p) is an anagram of `p`. Indices are in increasing order.
constraints: Both strings are lowercase English letters
hints: This is permutation-in-string, but you collect every matching index instead of returning early.
A fixed window of length len(p) is the only candidate size.
Update counts in O(1) per slide and compare the frequency vectors.

approaches.name: Sort each window
approaches.explanation: Compare sorted windows with sorted p.

approaches.name: Sliding counts
approaches.explanation: Record the left index whenever the counters match.

editorial: Build the frequency of p and of the first window. Whenever they match, record index 0 or the current left index. Then slide: add the new character, remove the character that falls off, and compare again.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def find_anagrams(s: str, p: str) -> list[int]:
    if len(p) > len(s):
        return []
    need = Counter(p)
    window = Counter(s[: len(p)])
    out: list[int] = []
    if window == need:
        out.append(0)
    width = len(p)
    for right in range(width, len(s)):
        window[s[right]] += 1
        left_ch = s[right - width]
        window[left_ch] -= 1
        if window[left_ch] == 0:
            del window[left_ch]
        if window == need:
            out.append(right - width + 1)
    return out
